core_obligations: Build the specialising sets (proof lines 15087-15091): the closed subsets Z_i of Z are quasi-compact, so the set W_i of points of X specialising to Z_i is closed in the constructible topology; assumption (2) implies X = W_1 coproduct W_2 as sets.

Show the W_i are closed in X (proof lines 15092-15096): if x lies in the closure of W_1, the specialisation lemma produces x_1 in W_1 with x_1 specialising to x, whence the closure of x is contained in the closure of x_1 and therefore x lies in W_1; hence setting X_i = W_i gives the required decomposition with Z_i = Z cap X_i.
proof_roadmap: Use quasi-compactness of the pieces to get constructible-closed specialising sets that partition X by the connectedness hypothesis.
Use the specialisation lemma to prove that each part is closed in X, giving the decomposition.
difficulty_reason: The lemma extends a decomposition of a closed subset with connected intersections with closures to a decomposition of the whole spectral space (statement lines 15071-15084). The proof (proof lines 15086-15096) forms the sets of points specialising to each piece, shows they are closed in the constructible topology and partition X, and then uses the specialisation lemma to show they are closed in X. H2: two short topological arguments, written out.
